policy.purpose: Classify the main LT verifier bundles without running them automatically.
policy.default_rule: Use the lowest tier that proves the claim; do not treat a passing local bundle as live readiness.
policy.execution_rule: Follow LT AGENTS.md, Frappe Cloud, Cloudflare, Stripe, email, and customer-data gates before running non-local checks.

tiers.tier_1_local_fast: Local lint, parser, unit, or shape checks with no external service.
tiers.tier_2_local_integrated: Local integration checks that may require local app services or local test records.
tiers.tier_3_staging_or_private: Staging, private platform, sandbox, or authenticated non-live checks.
tiers.tier_4_live_or_external: Live, customer-facing, publish, billing, public account, marketplace, deployment, or other external-impact gates.

bundles.scope: local browser contract for the shared public inquiry form experience
bundles.approval_required: no, when run only against the local developer app
risk_triggers: using a staging or live BaseUrl
proves: local UI contract for the public form path
bundles.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove live email delivery, live ERPNext persistence, Frappe Cloud settings, or customer-facing release readiness.

bundles.command: python .\scripts\verify\smoke_forms.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8081 --skip-newsletter && python .\scripts\verify\inquiry_spam_gate.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8081 && python .\scripts\verify\inquiry_sales_solicitation_filter.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8081
bundles.scope: local backend contract for inquiry intake, spam guard, and sales-solicitation suppression
bundles.environment: local Frappe app with local test data only
bundles.mutation: local test inquiry or Lead records may be created
bundles.approval_required: yes, because this can create local CRM/form test records
risk_triggers: claiming email delivery or inbox receipt
proves: local public form backend guard behavior
bundles.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove customer email receipt, live anti-spam health, or Frappe Cloud route configuration.

bundles.environment: local app unless AGENTS.md authorizes another target
bundles.approval_required: no, when run only against the local developer app
risk_triggers: Cloudflare or Frappe Cloud route proof
bundles.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove DNS, CDN, cache, live Frappe Cloud settings, or external customer access.

bundles.scope: local ecommerce, cart, checkout, product, and fulfillment contract bundle
bundles.environment: local app and local ecommerce test state only
bundles.mutation: local cart, checkout, and test commerce state may be touched
bundles.approval_required: yes, because this touches checkout and commerce-state surfaces even when local
proves: local ecommerce contract behavior across the named npm bundle
bundles.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove payment capture, Stripe live readiness, public sellability on production, or launch approval.

bundles.command: manual-gate: use capabilities/recipes/frappe-cloud-cloudflare-stripe-launch-gate.md and the active launch workstream
bundles.scope: Frappe Cloud, Cloudflare, Stripe, email, ecommerce fallback, and live cutover approval
bundles.environment: staging, live, and external provider accounts
bundles.mutation: may change external account, routing, payment, or live release state if approved
bundles.approval_required: yes, explicit project and account-context approval required every time
proves: only the approved launch-gate evidence named in the workstream after it is actually run
bundles.what_it_does_not_prove: The manifest itself proves nothing; it only marks this as a live/external approval boundary.

bundles.scope: read-only Wardenclyffe Kubuntu branch, tool, container, route, version, and app-order health check
bundles.environment: local files and local Docker only
proves: local Kubuntu runtime preconditions are present for further verification
bundles.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove layout quality, form persistence, checkout behavior, provider readiness, or live launch approval.

bundles.scope: read-only Meta Business, ad account, Page identity, campaigns, ad sets, ads, pixels, system users, insights endpoint, and Page-token lane blockers
bundles.environment: live Meta Graph API using local uncommitted token from .env or shell environment
bundles.approval_required: yes, because this touches a live external social/ad provider account even when read-only
risk_triggers: running against a different business or ad account
changing campaigns, spend, billing, pixels, datasets, posts, or Page settings
proves: the local token can perform the named read-only Meta inventory checks at the time it runs
required ad-account inventory access is present
Page post and lead-form lanes still need Page-token handling when blocked
bundles.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not approve or perform live changes, prove billing ownership, export leads, read messages, publish posts, create campaigns, change spend, alter ENB access, or prove future token validity.
